did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ezekiel’s vision in chapter 8 takes place in the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth day of the month, while Ezekiel is sitting in his house and the elders of Judah are sitting before him.
Did you know? Ezekiel describes a figure whose appearance is like fire: from the waist down it looks like fire, and from the waist up it looks radiant, like glowing amber.
Did you know? In the vision, Ezekiel is lifted by the Spirit between earth and heaven and brought to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the inner gate facing north.
Did you know? Although the vision exposes the people’s sins in the temple, Ezekiel still sees there the glory of the God of Israel, just as he had previously seen it in the plain.
Did you know? Near the altar gate, to the north, Ezekiel sees the “image of jealousy”—an image or sight that provokes the Lord’s jealousy, according to the chapter’s description.

Did you know? Ezekiel discovers the abominations in a hidden room after digging through the wall and finding an opening. This emphasizes the contrast between outward appearances and deeds carried out in secret.
Did you know? Seventy elders of the house of Israel are standing in the hidden room, including Jaazaniah son of Shaphan. Each man is holding a censer, and the smoke of the incense is rising.
Did you know? The elders say in their hearts that the Lord does not see them and that he has abandoned the land. Yet the vision itself shows that their secret deeds are visible to him.
Did you know? At the north gate of the house of the Lord, Ezekiel sees women sitting and mourning for Tammuz, as part of the series of abominations he is told to observe.
Did you know? In the inner court, Ezekiel sees about twenty-five men with their backs toward the temple of the Lord and their faces toward the east, bowing down to the sun.
